The long quote and the short note

Every long quotation carries a small debt: the reader has to know where it stops[1].

Footnotes solve the problem by leaving a marker in the flow and the full reference at the end[2].

The marker is small on purpose. It should be visible enough to be followed and quiet enough not to interrupt the sentence.

  1. Style guides differ on the exact placement of the marker.
  2. A note may itself cite another work, but not in this example.
